page: Microsoft Azure E8pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epdsv6 server family. It is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM architecture running at 3.4 GHz. The processor features 64 KB of L1D cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 472 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong, placing in the top 25% at 33.15 GB/sec. Most other compute benchmarks, including stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, Geekbench scores, and Redis SET operations, fall within the average range. However, the hardware exhibits performance limitations in specific areas: the Passmark CPU encryption test is weak (bottom 25%), and large language model inference speeds are low, with 7B model prompt processing categorized as poor (bottom 10%).

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E8pds_v6 offers high memory density and integrated NVMe storage on an ARM architecture, which typically provides a lower resource-to-cost profile compared to traditional x86 memory-optimized instances. The lack of hyperthreading and the presence of dedicated physical cores ensure predictable execution. This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and caching layers like Redis, while it is less suitable for cryptographic-heavy tasks or local LLM inference.
